name: Emulators and neural-network states for nuclear theory
summary: Eigenvector continuation and other reduced-basis emulators make Bayesian calibration of ab initio models affordable, and neural-network quantum states and NN-extrapolated no-core shell-model energies bring machine learning into the nuclear many-body problem.
breaks: Emulators interpolate within the training region and can fail where the ground state changes character.
sources: Frame et al. (2018). "Eigenvector Continuation with Subspace Learning". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 032501. [arXiv:1711.07090](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.07090)
Wolfgruber et al. (2024). "Precise neural network predictions of energies and radii from the no-core shell model". *Phys. Rev. C* 110, 014327. [arXiv:2310.05256](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05256)

name: Molecular dynamics of nuclear pasta and crust
summary: Classical and quantum molecular dynamics with screened-Coulomb plus nuclear potentials simulate millions of nucleons to find pasta shapes, defects, crust breaking strain and transport coefficients.
breaks: Semiclassical potentials miss shell effects and quantum degeneracy that can change pasta phase boundaries.
sources: Caplan & Horowitz (2017). "Colloquium: Astromaterial science and nuclear pasta". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 041002. [arXiv:1606.03646](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03646)

name: Monte Carlo was invented for neutron transport
summary: Ulam, von Neumann and Metropolis created the Monte Carlo method in 1946-49 to follow neutron chains in fissile assemblies; today MC neutron transport (MCNP, Serpent, OpenMC) computes reactor k_eff and the Metropolis algorithm spread across physics.
map: k_{\rm eff}=\frac{N_{\rm gen+1}}{N_{\rm gen}};\ p(s)=\Sigma_te^{-\Sigma_ts}\Rightarrow s=-\frac{\ln\xi}{\Sigma_t}
sources: Metropolis et al. (1953). "Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines". *J. Chem. Phys.* 21, 1087. [doi:10.1063/1.1699114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699114)

name: Monte Carlo radiation transport for detectors and dose
summary: Detector response, shielding and dose are computed with Monte Carlo transport of photons, electrons, neutrons and ions (Geant4, FLUKA, MCNP), sampling interaction cross sections particle by particle.
breaks: Accuracy is limited by cross-section data and condensed-history approximations for charged particles.
sources: Agostinelli et al. (2003). "Geant4—a simulation toolkit". *Nucl. Instrum. Methods A* 506, 250. [doi:10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8)

name: Monte Carlo jet-quenching event generators
summary: Medium-modified parton showers (JEWEL, MARTINI, MATTER/LBT in JETSCAPE) sample in-medium splitting and scattering stochastically inside an evolving QGP, extending collider event generators to heavy-ion jets.
breaks: Medium response and quantum interference (LPM) effects are implemented approximately and differ between generators.
sources: Cao et al. (2025). "Jet quenching: From theory to simulation". *Rep. Prog. Phys.*. [arXiv:2401.10026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10026)

name: Quantum Monte Carlo for nuclei
summary: Variational and Green's-function Monte Carlo and auxiliary-field diffusion Monte Carlo solve light nuclei and neutron matter by stochastic projection in imaginary time, sampling spin-isospin and spatial configurations.
breaks: The fermion sign problem forces constrained-path or fixed-node approximations as A grows.
sources: Carlson et al. (2015). "Quantum Monte Carlo methods for nuclear physics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 87, 1067. [arXiv:1412.3081](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3081)

name: Shock-capturing solvers for relativistic hydrodynamics
summary: Heavy-ion hydrodynamics codes (MUSIC and others) solve second-order viscous relativistic hydro with finite-volume, Kurganov-Tadmor shock-capturing schemes shared with astrophysical and numerical relativity codes.
breaks: Viscous relativistic hydro needs Israel-Stewart-type relaxation equations to remain causal, beyond standard conservation-law solvers.
sources: Schenke, Jeon & Gale (2010). "(3+1)D hydrodynamic simulation of relativistic heavy-ion collisions". *Phys. Rev. C* 82, 014903. [arXiv:1004.1408](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.1408)

name: Entanglement and DMRG in the nuclear shell model
summary: Mode entanglement between proton and neutron orbitals is low in many nuclei, which motivates DMRG and tensor-network truncations of shell-model spaces and entanglement-guided orbital ordering borrowed from quantum chemistry.
breaks: Nuclear orbitals have no natural 1D ordering and long-range quadrupole correlations raise entanglement, so DMRG gains are smaller than in 1D lattices.
sources: Pérez-Obiol et al. (2023). "Quantum entanglement patterns in the structure of atomic nuclei within the nuclear shell model". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 59, 240. [arXiv:2307.05197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05197)

name: Fission and the birth of big science
summary: The 1938-39 discovery and interpretation of fission (Hahn, Strassmann, Meitner, Frisch) led within six years to reactors and weapons, the Manhattan Project and the national-laboratory system that reshaped how physics is organized and funded.
sources: Meitner & Frisch (1939). "Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction". *Nature* 143, 239. [doi:10.1038/143239a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/143239a0)

name: Rutherford scattering and discovery of the nucleus
summary: Rutherford's 1911 analysis of alpha scattering revealed the nucleus and founded both nuclear physics and the scattering method that runs through particle and condensed-matter physics.
sources: Rutherford (1911). "The Scattering of α and β Particles by Matter and the Structure of the Atom". *Phil. Mag.* 21, 669. [doi:10.1080/14786440508637080](https://doi.org/10.1080/14786440508637080)

name: Nuclear EFT as a case study of levels and emergence
summary: Chiral EFT is a worked example in philosophy of physics of how autonomous effective levels relate to a deeper theory: nuclear physics is derivable from QCD in principle yet is organized by its own degrees of freedom, power counting and low-energy constants.
breaks: Philosophical readings (autonomy versus reduction) differ, and the derivation from QCD is only partial via lattice matching.
sources: Weinberg (1990). "Nuclear forces from chiral lagrangians". *Phys. Lett. B* 251, 288. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3)

name: Resonances as S-matrix poles and Coulomb functions
summary: Nuclear resonances are poles of the S-matrix on the unphysical sheet (Breit-Wigner, R-matrix, Gamow states), and charged-particle reactions and alpha decay use Coulomb wave functions and the Gamow factor from the analytic structure of the Coulomb problem.
breaks: Threshold effects and overlapping resonances make pole extraction model-dependent.
sources: Lane & Thomas (1958). "R-Matrix Theory of Nuclear Reactions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 30, 257. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.30.257](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.30.257)

name: Self-consistent Green's functions and optical potentials
summary: The self-consistent Green's function method computes nuclear spectral functions from Dyson's equation, and its self-energy is a microscopic nucleon-nucleus optical potential, uniting structure and reaction theory with propagator mathematics.
map: G=G^0+G^0\Sigma^\star G,\ \Sigma^\star(\mathbf r,\mathbf r';E)\leftrightarrow U_{\rm opt}(E);\ S(k,E)=-\tfrac1\pi\mathrm{Im}G
breaks: Truncations (ADC(n)) and three-body forces limit accuracy, and the optical potential's imaginary part needs a large model space.
sources: Dickhoff & Barbieri (2004). "Self-consistent Green's function method for nuclei and nuclear matter". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 52, 377. [arXiv:nucl-th/0402034](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0402034)

name: Shared detector electronics and noise limits
summary: Nuclear spectroscopy defined the charge-sensitive preamplifier, pulse shaping, photomultiplier and SiPM readout and the Fano and series/parallel noise analysis now generic to instrumentation.
breaks: Optimal shaping depends on detector capacitance and leakage; the noise model is generic but parameters are detector-specific.
sources: Fano (1947). "Ionization Yield of Radiations. II. The Fluctuations of the Number of Ions". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 26. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.26](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.26)

name: Bayesian extraction of QGP transport coefficients
summary: Temperature-dependent eta/s and zeta/s are inferred by Bayesian calibration of hydrodynamic models against flow data, with Gaussian-process emulators and posterior uncertainty, the same parameter-estimation machinery used in cosmology.
breaks: Posteriors depend on the model family (initial state, freeze-out), so systematic model uncertainty can dominate.
sources: Heffernan et al. (2024). "Bayesian quantification of strongly interacting matter with color glass condensate initial conditions". *Phys. Rev. C* 109, 065207. [arXiv:2302.09478](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.09478)

name: Bayesian multi-messenger inference of the dense-matter EOS
summary: The neutron-star EOS is inferred by Bayesian combination of chiral-EFT priors, heavy-pulsar masses, NICER pulse profiles and GW tidal deformabilities, using nonparametric (Gaussian-process, neural-network) EOS priors.
breaks: Prior choices at densities without data strongly shape posteriors on the maximum mass and quark-matter questions.
sources: Koehn et al. (2025). "From existing and new nuclear and astrophysical constraints to stringent limits on the equation of state of neutron-rich dense matter". *Phys. Rev. X* 15, 021014. [arXiv:2402.04172](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04172)

name: Neutron-lifetime puzzle and combining discrepant data
summary: Beam (about 888 s) and bottle (about 878 s) neutron lifetimes disagree by about 4 sigma; PDG scale factors, Birge ratios and Bayesian treatments of unknown systematics are used to combine them, and the choice matters for BBN and |V_ud|.
breaks: Statistics cannot decide whether a systematic error or new physics (dark decay channels) causes the gap.
sources: González-Alonso, Naviliat-Cuncic & Severijns (2019). "New physics searches in nuclear and neutron β decay". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 104, 165. [arXiv:1803.08732](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08732)

name: Bayesian EFT truncation errors for nuclear forces
summary: Chiral EFT predictions now carry theory error bars from Bayesian models of the omitted orders in Q/Lambda, treated as random coefficients with a learned scale, an EFT application of statistical inference.
map: y_k=y_{\rm ref}\sum_{n=0}^kc_nQ^n,\ \delta y_k\approx y_{\rm ref}\bar c\,\frac{Q^{k+1}}{\sqrt{1-Q^2}},\ c_n\sim\mathcal N(0,\bar c^2)
breaks: The assumption of natural, independent coefficients may fail when power counting is inconsistent.
sources: Furnstahl et al. (2015). "Quantifying truncation errors in effective field theory". *Phys. Rev. C* 92, 024005. [arXiv:1506.01343](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.01343)

name: Radioactive decay as the model Poisson process
summary: Radioactive decay is the textbook Poisson process: counts have variance equal to the mean, intervals are exponential, and counting statistics, dead-time and background subtraction are the reference examples of uncertainty propagation.
breaks: Detector dead time and electronics make observed counts sub-Poissonian, and very short-lived sources violate stationarity.

name: Neutron and nuclear EDMs as tests of T and CP
summary: A permanent electric dipole moment of the neutron or a nucleus violates P and T; the neutron EDM bound underlies the strong CP problem, and octupole-deformed nuclei such as 225Ra enhance Schiff moments by orders of magnitude.
breaks: Converting EDM limits to CP-violating parameters needs nuclear and hadronic matrix elements with large uncertainties.
sources: Abel et al. (2020). "Measurement of the Permanent Electric Dipole Moment of the Neutron". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 081803. [arXiv:2001.11966](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.11966)

name: Parity violation in nuclear beta decay
summary: Wu's 1957 measurement of the electron asymmetry from polarized 60Co showed the weak interaction maximally violates parity, establishing the V-A structure of beta decay.
sources: Wu et al. (1957). "Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay". *Phys. Rev.* 105, 1413. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.105.1413](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.105.1413)

name: Isospin and Wigner SU(4) symmetry of nuclear forces
summary: Charge independence of nuclear forces makes isospin an SU(2) symmetry with protons and neutrons as a doublet; Wigner's combined spin-isospin SU(4) supermultiplets explain why light-nucleus binding and Gamow-Teller patterns follow the 4-fold degeneracy.
breaks: Isospin is broken by Coulomb forces and the u-d quark mass difference (~1 percent), and SU(4) is broken strongly by spin-orbit forces in heavier nuclei.
sources: Heisenberg (1932). "Über den Bau der Atomkerne. I". *Z. Phys.* 77, 1. [doi:10.1007/BF01342433](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01342433)

Wigner (1937). "On the Consequences of the Symmetry of the Nuclear Hamiltonian on the Spectroscopy of Nuclei". *Phys. Rev.* 51, 106. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.51.106](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.51.106)

name: Elliott SU(3) and interacting-boson dynamical symmetries
summary: Collective rotation emerges from the shell model through Elliott's SU(3) for the harmonic oscillator, and the interacting boson model's U(6) group chains U(5), SU(3) and O(6) give the vibrational, rotational and gamma-soft limits of nuclear spectra.
breaks: Real nuclei lie between limits and spin-orbit coupling breaks Elliott SU(3) beyond the sd shell (pseudo- and quasi-SU(3) partly restore it).
sources: Elliott (1958). "Collective motion in the nuclear shell model. I. Classification schemes for states of mixed configuration". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 245, 128. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1958.0072](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1958.0072)

Arima & Iachello (1976). "Interacting boson model of collective states I. The vibrational limit". *Ann. Phys.* 99, 253. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(76)90097-x](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(76)90097-x)

name: Seniority and quasispin: pairing as an SU(2) algebra
summary: Racah's seniority scheme and Kerman's quasispin show that pair creation and annihilation in a j-shell close an SU(2) algebra, which makes the pairing Hamiltonian exactly solvable and explains constant 2+ energies in semi-magic nuclei.
breaks: Seniority is exact only in a single j-shell or with degenerate orbits; multi-j shells and quadrupole forces mix seniorities.
sources: Racah (1943). "Theory of Complex Spectra. III". *Phys. Rev.* 63, 367. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.63.367](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.63.367)

name: Conserved vector current and superallowed ft values
summary: The vector weak current is the Noether current of isospin (CVC), so Fermi matrix elements of superallowed 0+ to 0+ decays are fixed by symmetry; after small isospin-breaking and radiative corrections all ft values agree, which tests CVC and gives |V_ud|.
breaks: Isospin-breaking corrections delta_C are model-dependent and are the leading theory uncertainty.
sources: Feynman & Gell-Mann (1958). "Theory of the Fermi Interaction". *Phys. Rev.* 109, 193. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.109.193](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.109.193)

Hardy & Towner (2020). "Superallowed 0+→0+ nuclear β decays: 2020 critical survey, with implications for Vud and CKM unitarity". *Phys. Rev. C* 102, 045501. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501)

name: Chiral restoration and O(4) universality
summary: The QCD transition is chiral-symmetry restoration; Pisarski and Wilczek argued that for two massless flavours it falls in the 3D O(4) universality class, and lattice data at physical masses show a crossover with O(4) scaling remnants.
breaks: Explicit quark masses turn the transition into a crossover, and the U(1)_A anomaly strength affects the universality class.
sources: Pisarski & Wilczek (1984). "Remarks on the chiral phase transition in chromodynamics". *Phys. Rev. D* 29, 338. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.29.338](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.29.338)

name: Pions as Goldstone bosons organize nuclear forces
summary: Spontaneous breaking of QCD's chiral SU(2)xSU(2) symmetry makes pions light pseudo-Goldstone bosons with derivative couplings; this fixes one-pion exchange as the long-range nuclear force and Weinberg's power counting in Q/Lambda_chi.
map: SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R\to SU(2)_V;\ m_\pi^2f_\pi^2=-(m_u+m_d)\langle\bar qq\rangle;\ V_{1\pi}\propto\frac{g_A^2}{f_\pi^2}\frac{(\sigma_1\cdot q)(\sigma_2\cdot q)}{q^2+m_\pi^2}
breaks: Nonperturbative NN binding forces iteration of the potential, and power-counting consistency in that regime is debated.
sources: Weinberg (1990). "Nuclear forces from chiral lagrangians". *Phys. Lett. B* 251, 288. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3)
Epelbaum, Hammer & Meißner (2009). "Modern theory of nuclear forces". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1773. [arXiv:0811.1338](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1338)

name: Nuclear deformation and pairing as broken symmetries
summary: Deformed mean fields break rotational symmetry and BCS pairing breaks particle number; in finite nuclei the broken symmetry shows up as rotational bands (Anderson-tower rotations) and pairing rotations, restored by projection.
map: E_J=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\mathcal I}J(J+1)\ \text{(rotational tower)};\ E_{\rm pair\ rot}\propto\frac{(N-N_0)^2}{2\mathcal I_{\rm pair}}
breaks: A finite system cannot truly break a continuous symmetry; the 'Goldstone modes' are discrete rotational excitations whose spacing shrinks only as A grows.
sources: Bender, Heenen & Reinhard (2003). "Self-consistent mean-field models for nuclear structure". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 121. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.75.121](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.75.121)

name: Taylor's blast-wave estimate of a fission yield
summary: G. I. Taylor estimated the energy of the first atomic explosion from photographs of the fireball radius versus time using only dimensional analysis, the classic Taylor-Sedov scaling.
breaks: Scaling fixes the yield only up to the dimensionless constant C(gamma), which needs a similarity solution.
sources: Taylor (1950). "The formation of a blast wave by a very intense explosion II. The atomic explosion of 1945". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 201, 175. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1950.0050](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1950.0050)

name: Oklo natural reactor bounds varying constants
summary: The 2-billion-year-old Oklo natural fission reactor depleted 149Sm through its 0.1 eV neutron resonance; the resonance position today matches, bounding changes of the fine-structure constant to about 1e-7 over that time.
breaks: The bound depends on modelling the reactor's neutron spectrum and temperature and on assuming only alpha varies.
sources: Shlyakhter (1976). "Direct test of the constancy of fundamental nuclear constants". *Nature* 264, 340. [doi:10.1038/264340a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/264340a0)

name: Proton radius and the Rydberg constant in CODATA
summary: The proton charge radius enters hydrogen energy levels, so it is adjusted jointly with the Rydberg constant; the muonic-hydrogen radius (0.84 fm) shifted the CODATA values of both after the proton-radius puzzle.
breaks: Electron-scattering extractions depend on form-factor fit extrapolation to Q^2 = 0.
sources: Pohl et al. (2010). "The size of the proton". *Nature* 466, 213. [doi:10.1038/nature09250](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09250)

Tiesinga et al. (2021). "CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 2018". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 93, 025010. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.93.025010](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.93.025010)

name: BBN constrains variation of constants
summary: Primordial helium and deuterium are sensitive to the neutron-proton mass difference, deuteron binding, G_F and G at T ~ 1 MeV, so BBN bounds variations of the fine-structure constant, quark masses and Newton's constant over 13.8 Gyr.
breaks: Correlated variations in unified theories make single-constant bounds model-dependent.
sources: Iocco et al. (2009). "Primordial Nucleosynthesis: from precision cosmology to fundamental physics". *Phys. Rep.* 472, 1. [arXiv:0809.0631](https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.0631)

name: Thorium-229 nuclear clock and variation of alpha
summary: The 8.4 eV 229Th isomer energy results from near-cancellation of MeV-scale Coulomb and nuclear energies, so a nuclear clock is predicted to be orders of magnitude more sensitive to drifts of the fine-structure constant and quark masses than atomic clocks.
breaks: The enhancement factor depends on the difference of Coulomb energies of two nuclear states, which is uncertain to a factor of a few.
sources: Flambaum (2006). "Enhanced Effect of Temporal Variation of the Fine Structure Constant and the Strong Interaction in 229Th". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 97, 092502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.092502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.092502)

name: Atomic masses, the mole and the 2019 SI
summary: Nuclear masses are measured as ratios to 12C (the unified atomic mass unit); Penning-trap mass ratios feed CODATA, and the 28Si-sphere Avogadro determination behind the new kilogram relied on isotopic enrichment and neutron-activation impurity analysis.
breaks: Since 2019 the mole is defined by a fixed N_A, so m_u is no longer exactly 1 g/mol divided by N_A.
sources: Wang et al. (2021). "The AME 2020 atomic mass evaluation (II). Tables, graphs and references". *Chinese Phys. C* 45, 030003. [doi:10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf](https://doi.org/10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf)

name: Nuclear rainbows from the classical deflection function
summary: Semiclassical (Ford–Wheeler) scattering identifies the WKB phase shift with the classical action, so the deflection function Θ(l) = 2 dδ_l/dl follows from orbits in the nuclear plus Coulomb potential. Where Θ has an extremum the classical cross section diverges, giving nuclear and Coulomb rainbows whose Airy patterns in light heavy-ion elastic scattering map the optical potential deep inside the nucleus.

name: Gamow factor as the action through the barrier
summary: The α-decay rate of Gamow and Gurney–Condon is a classical assault frequency v/2R times the WKB penetrability. Its exponent is the Hamilton–Jacobi action of the forbidden orbit under the Coulomb barrier, where the momentum is imaginary, and evaluating it gives the Geiger–Nuttall law; the same exponent sets the Gamow peak of stellar fusion.
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)
Gurney & Condon (1928). "Wave Mechanics and Radioactive Disintegration". *Nature* 122, 439. [doi:10.1038/122439a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/122439a0)

name: Vlasov/BUU transport as Hamiltonian phase-space flow
summary: Intermediate-energy collisions and hadronic afterburners are modelled with Boltzmann–Uehling–Uhlenbeck (Vlasov) transport. Hamilton's equations in the nuclear mean field carry the one-body phase-space density (Liouville flow, solved with test particles), plus Pauli-blocked collisions, and the directed and elliptic flow these simulations produce constrain the dense-matter equation of state.
map: \partial_t f+\{f,h[f]\}=I_{\rm coll}[f],\ \dot{\mathbf r}=\partial h/\partial\mathbf p,\ \dot{\mathbf p}=-\partial h/\partial\mathbf r

name: Bohr Hamiltonian: a quantized collective Lagrangian
summary: The Bohr collective model takes generalized coordinates (quadrupole deformation β, γ plus three Euler angles), writes a classical kinetic energy with a deformation-dependent mass tensor, and quantizes it in curved collective space with the Pauli prescription. Vibrator, γ-soft and rotor spectra are limits of this one Lagrangian.

name: Spontaneous fission along the least-action path
summary: Spontaneous-fission half-lives are computed by tunnelling through a multidimensional deformation landscape along the path that minimizes the WKB action. This is Jacobi's form of the Maupertuis principle in a collective space with a position-dependent inertia tensor, so the dynamical path differs from the static minimum-energy path.

name: Rayleigh–Ritz: from vibrating plates to nuclei
summary: The variational bound used throughout ab initio nuclear theory (variational Monte Carlo, truncated-basis no-core shell model, Hartree–Fock references) descends from Rayleigh's quotient for the frequencies of vibrating systems and Ritz's 1909 method for elastic plates. The quantum Rayleigh–Ritz principle is the same eigenvalue minimization.

name: Pressure and shear inside the proton
summary: The gravitational form factors of the energy–momentum tensor (including the D-term) are read as a continuum-mechanics stress tensor: a radial pressure p(r) and shear force s(r) inside the proton, with von Laue's equilibrium condition ∫p r² dr = 0 and a mechanical radius. First extractions came from deeply virtual Compton scattering, and the EIC will map them.
breaks: Local 3D densities of a relativistic, recoiling bound state depend on the frame (Breit frame vs light front), and whether p(r) is a physical pressure is debated.

name: Love numbers: from Earth tides to Lambda
summary: The tidal deformability measured from GW170817's inspiral phase is built on the Love number k_2, which A. E. H. Love introduced for the elastic tidal response of the Earth. For a neutron star k_2 measures how centrally condensed the fluid is, so the measurement bounds EOS stiffness and radius.
breaks: The neutron-star k_2 is a relativistic fluid response computed from perturbed TOV equations. Crust rigidity contributes negligibly, unlike the Earth's elastic Love numbers.

name: Neutron-star crust as an elastic solid
summary: The neutron-star crust is a Coulomb crystal whose shear modulus is set by the nuclear charges and lattice spacing. Its elastic response governs starquakes and crust breaking, the largest 'mountain' that could radiate continuous gravitational waves, and the torsional shear modes proposed for magnetar-flare QPOs.

name: Heavy-ion fireballs as relativistic viscous fluids
summary: Navier–Stokes hydrodynamics, made relativistic and causal (Israel–Stewart, second order), is the standard model of the heavy-ion fireball: pressure gradients turn the almond-shaped overlap into elliptic flow v_2, and fits to v_n extract the shear viscosity much as viscous damping is measured in a classical flow. Bjorken's boost-invariant expansion is an exact similarity solution of these equations.
sources: Bjorken (1983). "Highly relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions: The central rapidity region". *Phys. Rev. D* 27, 140. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.27.140](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.27.140)

name: QCD critical point in the liquid–gas dynamic class
summary: Near the conjectured QCD critical point the slow modes are diffusive baryon density coupled to shear flow, exactly as at a liquid–gas critical point. That places it in Hohenberg–Halperin Model H, with the same critical slowing down, divergent conductivity and bulk-viscosity peak, and fluctuating hydrodynamics is used to predict the proton-cumulant signals.
map: \tau_{\rm relax}\sim\xi^{z},\ z\approx3\ (\text{Model H, as for a classical liquid–gas critical point})

name: Perfect liquid: eta/s of the QGP vs ordinary fluids
summary: Shear viscosity, defined by Newton's law of viscous stress, is compared across fluids through η/s, the relativistic analogue of kinematic viscosity. The QGP sits near ħ/4πk_B, about an order of magnitude below helium, nitrogen or water at their minima, which makes it the most nearly ideal (Euler) fluid known.
breaks: Kinetic theory gives η ∼ ρ v̄ λ (mean free path), which loses meaning at strong coupling where there are no quasiparticles. The 1/4π value is a holographic result for idealized gauge theories, not a proven lower bound.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

name: Irrotational and viscous liquid-drop fission dynamics
summary: The descent from saddle to scission is modelled as flow of an incompressible nuclear fluid. Irrotational (Werner–Wheeler) flow gives the collective inertia, and adding two-body viscosity through Navier–Stokes (Davies–Sierk–Nix) slows the descent, stretches the neck and lowers fragment kinetic energies. Measured kinetic energies and prescission neutrons calibrate the dissipation.
breaks: Nuclear dissipation is mostly one-body (nucleons hitting the moving surface), not two-body viscosity, because the nucleon mean free path is comparable to the nuclear size.

name: Convective mixing sets s- and i-process yields
summary: Neutron-capture nucleosynthesis depends on classical fluid instabilities. In AGB stars, partial mixing at convective boundaries forms the ¹³C pocket that powers the main s-process, convective-reactive ingestion of hydrogen into helium-burning zones drives the i-process, and in core-collapse supernovae Rayleigh–Taylor fingers carry fresh ⁵⁶Ni outward, as seen in SN 1987A.

name: Fission as Rayleigh's charged-drop instability
summary: Bohr–Wheeler fission is Rayleigh's instability of a charged liquid drop: surface tension restores and Coulomb repulsion drives the quadrupole mode, and the sphere loses stability when E_C = 2E_S (fissility x = 1). Because the liquid-drop barrier vanishes for the heaviest nuclei, they survive only through shell corrections, and the final neck rupture parallels Rayleigh–Plateau pinch-off.
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)
Meitner & Frisch (1939). "Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction". *Nature* 143, 239. [doi:10.1038/143239a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/143239a0)

name: Heavy quarks as Brownian particles in the QGP
summary: Charm and bottom quarks (M ≫ T) random-walk through the QGP like colloids in a viscous liquid. A Langevin equation with drag and momentum diffusion, tied together by the Einstein relation, describes their thermalization, and the spatial diffusion coefficient extracted from heavy-flavour R_AA and v_2 is a key transport parameter.
breaks: Stokes drag 6πηa assumes a continuum fluid around a large sphere. The heavy quark is pointlike, comparable to the medium's interparticle spacing, and its drag comes from colour interactions with relativistic corrections, not from viscous boundary layers.

name: Jet energy loss as a wave-turbulent gluon cascade
summary: Medium-induced radiation from a jet in the QGP becomes a cascade of democratic gluon branchings. It carries energy at a constant rate from the leading parton to soft gluons and into the medium, with a Kolmogorov–Zakharov fixed-point spectrum, which explains why the lost energy reappears at large angles.
map: D(x)\propto x^{-1/2}\ (\text{KZ fixed point})\ \leftrightarrow\ E(k)\propto k^{-5/3}
breaks: The cascade is in the energy fraction x of a branching process, not in a 3D velocity field. Its flux is set by \hat q and the path length, and the inertial range ends at the medium temperature.
sources: Kolmogorov (1941; English translation 1991). "The local structure of turbulence in incompressible viscous fluid for very large Reynolds numbers". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 434, 9. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1991.0075](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1991.0075)

name: Turbulent cascade in early QGP thermalization
summary: Before hydrodynamics applies, the over-occupied gluon fields left by the collision thermalize through a self-similar, constant-flux energy cascade toward high momenta. This is a Kolmogorov–Zakharov-type wave turbulence (a non-thermal fixed point), the same idea as the Richardson–Kolmogorov cascade in fluids.
breaks: The cascade runs in the momentum space of weakly coupled classical gluon fields. Its exponents come from the kinetic collision term, not K41's −5/3, and there are no spatial eddies and no Navier–Stokes nonlinearity.

name: Bohr's classical stopping power
summary: Bohr's 1913 stopping theory is impulse-approximation Coulomb scattering: a fast ion passing an electron at impact parameter b gives it Δp = 2Ze²/(4πε0 b v). Integrating over b between a close-collision cutoff and the adiabatic cutoff v/ω gives the logarithmic energy loss that Bethe later made quantum, the basis of range–energy relations, Bragg peaks and detector response.

name: Rutherford scattering: a hyperbolic orbit found the nucleus
summary: Geiger–Marsden α scattering was explained by classical hyperbolic orbits in a repulsive 1/r potential. Rutherford's cross section is also exact in quantum mechanics, deviations from it still show where the nuclear force begins (closest approach, Coulomb barrier), and for heavy ions with Sommerfeld parameter η ≫ 1 classical trajectories stay quantitative.

name: Shell structure from closed classical orbits
summary: By Bertrand's theorem only the oscillator and Kepler potentials have every bound orbit closed, and that classical degeneracy is why the oscillator gives large shell gaps at 2, 8, 20, 40. In realistic wells, periodic-orbit theory (Balian–Bloch, Strutinsky, the Gutzwiller trace formula) writes the oscillating level density, the shell correction behind magic numbers and superheavy stability, as a sum over the shortest closed orbits.
map: \delta g(E)=\sum_{\rm po}A_{\rm po}\cos\left(\frac{S_{\rm po}}{\hbar}-\sigma_{\rm po}\frac\pi2\right),\ S_{\rm po}=\oint\mathbf p\cdot d\mathbf q
breaks: Spin–orbit coupling, essential for the magic numbers 28, 50, 82 and 126, needs spin-dependent extensions of the trace formula.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)

name: Neutron moderation by elastic-collision kinematics
summary: Slowing fission neutrons to thermal energy is pure two-body elastic-collision kinematics. Momentum and energy conservation fix the maximum fractional energy loss on a nucleus of mass number A and the mean logarithmic decrement ξ, which is why light nuclei moderate best: about 18 collisions on hydrogen against about 115 on carbon to go from 2 MeV to 0.025 eV.

name: Neutrino invented to save conservation laws
summary: The continuous β spectrum, together with the spin–statistics bookkeeping of the nuclei, seemed to break conservation of energy and angular momentum, and Bohr considered giving up energy conservation. Pauli instead postulated a light neutral spin-½ particle, which Fermi built into his theory of β decay: a conservation law predicting a particle.
map: Q=T_e+T_{\bar\nu}+T_{\rm rec},\ \textstyle\sum\mathbf p=0,\ \Delta J\ \text{balanced only with a spin-}\tfrac12\ \bar\nu
sources: Fermi (1934). "Versuch einer Theorie der β-Strahlen. I". *Z. Phys.* 88, 161. [doi:10.1007/BF01351864](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01351864)

name: Chadwick weighed the neutron with collision kinematics
summary: Chadwick identified the neutron by comparing the maximum recoil velocities of hydrogen and nitrogen nuclei struck by the unknown radiation. Head-on elastic-collision kinematics gave a neutral particle with about the proton's mass, and ruled out the γ-ray hypothesis, which needed implausibly high photon energies.
sources: Chadwick (1932). "Possible Existence of a Neutron". *Nature* 129, 312. [doi:10.1038/129312a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/129312a0)

name: Neutron-star masses from binary orbits
summary: Every neutron-star mass that constrains the EOS comes from binary celestial mechanics: Keplerian elements and the mass function, plus post-Keplerian effects (periastron advance, Shapiro delay) to break degeneracies. Demorest et al. used the Shapiro delay to measure a 2 M_⊙ pulsar, which rules out soft EOSs.
sources: Demorest et al. (2010). "A two-solar-mass neutron star measured using Shapiro delay". *Nature* 467, 1081. [doi:10.1038/nature09466](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09466)

name: Vortical fireball: spin polarization from rotation
summary: Off-central collisions carry enormous orbital angular momentum, and the fluid's thermal vorticity (about 10^22 s^-1, the most vortical fluid known) polarizes Λ hyperons along it. The equilibrium density matrix is the rotating-frame one, so spin aligns with ω as in the Barnett effect.

name: r-modes: Coriolis-restored waves that spin stars down
summary: The r-modes of a rotating star are Rossby waves with the Coriolis force as their restoring force. Gravitational radiation drives them unstable (Chandrasekhar–Friedman–Schutz) unless the shear and bulk viscosity of dense matter damp them, so the observed spins of fast pulsars constrain neutron-star viscosity and composition.

name: Cranking model: nuclei in the rotating frame
summary: Inglis's cranking model solves the nucleon problem in a frame rotating at ω. Its Routhian H' = H − ωJ_x contains the Coriolis and centrifugal terms and yields moments of inertia, and the Coriolis force breaking high-j pairs and aligning their spins explains backbending in yrast bands.
map: H'=H-\omega J_x,\ \mathcal I^{(1)}=\frac{\langle J_x\rangle}{\omega}\ \leftrightarrow\ \mathbf F_{\rm Cor}=-2m\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf v

name: Rotating-drop shape bifurcations (Maclaurin–Jacobi)
summary: A rotating charged liquid drop follows the classical sequence of rotating fluid masses. Oblate axisymmetric shapes bifurcate into triaxial Jacobi-like shapes at a critical angular momentum, and the fission barrier vanishes at higher spin. Cohen, Plasil and Swiatecki mapped these sequences for nuclei, and a Jacobi shape transition has been reported in hot, fast-rotating nuclei through GDR splitting.
breaks: Surface tension replaces self-gravity, so the sequences differ quantitatively from the Maclaurin–Jacobi ones. Quantized angular momentum, shell effects (superdeformed bands) and pairing modify the classical drop.

name: Wall-formula dissipation needs chaotic nucleon billiards
summary: One-body dissipation treats nucleons as a gas bouncing inside a moving container (the wall-and-window formula of Błocki, Swiatecki and co-workers). Classical billiard simulations showed that the full wall-formula damping holds only when particle motion in the container shape is chaotic and is much weaker for integrable shapes, which ties fission damping to classical chaos.
map: \dot E=\rho\bar v\oint\dot n^2\,dS\ (\text{full strength only for chaotic billiards})

name: Compound-nucleus resonances and quantum chaos
summary: Neutron-resonance spacings in compound nuclei (the Nuclear Data Ensemble) follow the Wigner–Dyson GOE statistics that Wigner introduced for nuclei. The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture ties such spectra to classically chaotic Hamiltonian dynamics, while regular (KAM-integrable) systems give Poisson statistics, so the 'forgetting' assumed by Bohr's compound nucleus and Hauser–Feshbach theory is an ergodicity statement.

name: Skyrmions: baryons as topological solitons
summary: In the Skyrme model, which the large-N_c limit of QCD motivates, the chiral pion Lagrangian supports stable topological solitons whose winding number is baryon number. Nucleons, nuclei and nuclear matter appear as classical field configurations quantized through their collective rotations, carrying the soliton idea from classical nonlinear waves into the strong force.
breaks: Skyrmions are topological solitons, not integrable ones: there is no inverse scattering and they deform when they interact. The model overbinds light nuclei and has been superseded quantitatively by chiral EFT.

name: Surface vibrations: Rayleigh drop modes quantized
summary: Quadrupole and octupole phonons in vibrational nuclei are the quantized normal modes of a charged liquid drop's surface, R(θ,φ) = R_0[1 + Σ α_λμ Y_λμ]. The restoring constant combines surface tension and Coulomb terms as in Rayleigh's capillary-oscillation analysis, which predicts two-phonon 0+, 2+, 4+ triplets near 2ħω.
breaks: Measured mass parameters exceed irrotational-flow values, many supposedly vibrational nuclei miss the harmonic two-phonon pattern, and shell structure rather than surface tension sets most low-lying collectivity.
sources: Weizsäcker (1935). "Zur Theorie der Kernmassen". *Z. Phys.* 96, 431. [doi:10.1007/BF01337700](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01337700)

name: Superdeformation from 2:1 oscillator resonance
summary: In the deformed (Nilsson) oscillator, whenever ω_⊥:ω_z is a ratio of small integers the classical orbits close into Lissajous figures and the quantum levels bunch into degenerate shells. The 2:1 resonance produces the superdeformed magic numbers and 3:1 gives hyperdeformation, the same commensurability that makes classical oscillator orbits periodic.

name: Giant resonances as acoustic modes of nucleon fluids
summary: In the giant dipole resonance protons oscillate against neutrons. Goldhaber–Teller model it as two rigid spheres sloshing (E ∝ A^{-1/6}), Steinwedel–Jensen as a standing sound wave of isovector density in a fixed sphere (E ∝ A^{-1/3}), and the data interpolate between them; the isoscalar monopole breathing mode measures nuclear incompressibility.
map: E_{\rm SJ}\propto A^{-1/3},\ E_{\rm GT}\propto A^{-1/6};\ E_{\rm GMR}=\hbar\sqrt{K_A/(m\langle r^2\rangle)}
breaks: Nuclear sound is zero sound of a Fermi liquid (Fermi-surface distortion at ωτ ≫ 1), not collisional first sound, and the resonances are Landau-damped into particle–hole states.

name: Wobbling: quantized precession of a triaxial top
summary: A triaxial nucleus with three distinct moments of inertia is a quantum asymmetric top. Bohr–Mottelson wobbling is the quantized small-amplitude precession of the rotation axis about the axis of largest inertia, the stable branch of Euler's tennis-racket analysis, and wobbling bands have been seen in odd-A Lu isotopes.
map: \omega_{\rm wob}=\omega_{\rm rot}\sqrt{\frac{(\mathcal I_1-\mathcal I_2)(\mathcal I_1-\mathcal I_3)}{\mathcal I_2\mathcal I_3}}\ \leftrightarrow\ \text{Euler small-oscillation frequency}
breaks: The moment hierarchy is set by quantum (irrotational-like) flow. An aligned high-j quasiparticle (transverse wobbling) changes the classical stability criterion, and some wobbling assignments are disputed.

name: Neutron-star moment of inertia and glitches
summary: Pulsar spin-down, glitches and binary spin–orbit precession are rotational dynamics of a two-component body. A glitch transfers angular momentum from a superfluid component to the crust, so the crust's share of the moment of inertia constrains the EOS, and EOS-insensitive I–Love–Q relations tie the moment of inertia to tidal deformability and quadrupole.
sources: Lattimer & Prakash (2001). "Neutron star structure and the equation of state". *Astrophys. J.* 550, 426. [arXiv:astro-ph/0002232](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0002232)

name: Rotational bands: the quantized rotor and its inertia
summary: Deformed nuclei show bands E_J = ħ²J(J+1)/2𝓘, the spectrum of a quantized free rotor with E(4+)/E(2+) = 10/3. The moment of inertia is the classical quantity, and its measured value, which lies between the irrotational-flow and rigid-body values, directly probes nuclear superfluidity.
map: E_J=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\mathcal I}J(J+1)\leftrightarrow T=\frac{L^2}{2I},\quad \mathcal I_{\rm irr}<\mathcal I_{\rm exp}<\mathcal I_{\rm rig}
breaks: There is no collective rotation about a symmetry axis (quantum indistinguishability). 𝓘 is far from rigid: pairing reduces it to roughly 30–50% of the rigid value, and it changes with spin (Coriolis anti-pairing, backbending).

name: Coherent vs incoherent diffraction as speckle statistics
summary: In diffractive vector-meson production off nuclei, the coherent cross section is the square of the configuration-averaged amplitude and the incoherent part is its variance (Good–Walker). This is the same split as specular versus diffuse speckle scattering in the statistical optics of random media. The coherent t-spectrum images the average gluon density and the incoherent one its event-by-event fluctuations, a key saturation probe at the EIC.
breaks: The average runs over quantum configurations of nucleons and gluon hot spots in the target, not over a classical ensemble of scatterers. Saturation also makes the amplitude non-linear in the density.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: HBT intensity interferometry becomes femtoscopy
summary: Hanbury Brown–Twiss intensity interferometry was invented to measure stellar diameters and became femtoscopy in nuclear physics. Two-pion Bose–Einstein correlations (the GGLP effect, 1960) measure the space-time size of the emitting source, and the HBT radii R_out, R_side and R_long test hydrodynamic expansion and freeze-out. The 'HBT puzzle' (R_out/R_side ≈ 1, against early hydro predictions) was resolved by improved hydrodynamic modelling.
map: C_2(\mathbf q)=1+\lambda|\tilde S(\mathbf q)|^2\approx1+\lambda e^{-R_o^2q_o^2-R_s^2q_s^2-R_l^2q_l^2}\ \leftrightarrow\ g^{(2)}=1+|g^{(1)}|^2
breaks: Stellar HBT measures the spatial coherence of light from a static, distant source. Femtoscopy uses massive identical hadrons from an expanding source, so it measures homogeneity regions tied to the flow, needs Coulomb and strong final-state corrections, and gives anticorrelations for fermions.

name: Nucleon tomography from GPDs
summary: Fourier-transforming generalized parton distributions over transverse momentum transfer gives impact-parameter densities. Exclusive processes at the EIC therefore work as a tomograph that images quarks and gluons in the transverse plane at each momentum fraction x. Interference of DVCS with the calculable Bethe–Heitler amplitude supplies the phase, playing the role of a holographic reference wave.
breaks: What is imaged is a distribution in x and b_⊥ (or a Wigner quasi-distribution), not a real-space picture. GPDs enter observables through convolution integrals that cannot be uniquely inverted, unlike an optical Fourier transform.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: Form factors as Fourier transforms of charge density
summary: In the Born approximation, the elastic electron-scattering form factor is the Fourier transform of the charge density, just as the Fraunhofer amplitude is the Fourier transform of an aperture. Hofstadter's diffraction minima mapped nuclear charge distributions, and the slope at Q^2=0 gives the rms radius. The Sachs form factors G_E and G_M extend this to the nucleon.
map: F(\mathbf q)=\int\rho(\mathbf r)e^{i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf r}d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ U(\mathbf k_\perp)\propto\int A(\mathbf x)e^{-i\mathbf k_\perp\cdot\mathbf x}d^2x;\ \ \langle r_E^2\rangle=-6\frac{dG_E}{dQ^2}\Big|_0
breaks: For the nucleon, size and Compton wavelength are comparable, so recoil spoils the 3D Breit-frame Fourier interpretation; only 2D transverse densities in the infinite-momentum frame are rigorous. Two-photon exchange also breaks the one-photon (Born) picture and is the leading explanation of the Rosenbluth versus polarization-transfer discrepancy.

name: Neutron optics: refractive index from scattering length
summary: Slow neutrons travel through matter with a refractive index n = 1 − λ^2 N b_c/2π set by the coherent nuclear scattering length, so they refract and are totally reflected below a critical angle. Neutron guides and supermirrors at research reactors and spallation sources, and ultracold-neutron storage bottles, are built on this geometric optics. The Fermi pseudopotential 2πħ^2 N b_c/m is the zero-energy limit of the nuclear optical potential.
breaks: For most materials n < 1, so the reflection is external rather than internal. The index scales as λ^2 instead of following an electronic resonance, and gravity and absorption visibly bend and weaken the beams.

name: Glauber diffraction theory to Glauber initial states
summary: Glauber's eikonal multiple-scattering theory extended Fresnel–Kirchhoff diffraction to composite targets through the profile function 1 − e^{iχ}. Its Monte Carlo descendant gives the participant number, binary-collision number and initial eccentricities that seed every hydrodynamic flow calculation. The same Roy Glauber founded the quantum theory of optical coherence.
map: \Gamma(\mathbf b)=1-e^{i\chi(\mathbf b)},\ \ f(\mathbf q)=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int d^2b\,e^{i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf b}\Gamma(\mathbf b);\ \ N_{\rm coll}=\sigma_{NN}^{\rm inel}T_{AB}(b)
breaks: The Monte Carlo Glauber model used for flow keeps only the geometric overlap of nucleons and the inelastic NN cross section. It drops the wave-optical phases of the original theory.

name: Nuclear diffraction scattering and the black disk
summary: High-energy hadron and α scattering on nuclei shows the Fraunhofer pattern of an absorbing disk, with minima at kRθ ≈ 3.83 and 7.02. The total cross section is σ_tot = 2πR^2, half elastic shadow and half absorption, which is the extinction paradox of optics. Coulomb-dominated heavy-ion scattering (large Sommerfeld parameter η) shows Fresnel diffraction and nuclear rainbows instead.

name: Optical pumping for polarized nuclear targets and beams
summary: Circularly polarized laser light transfers angular momentum to atoms. Spin-exchange optical pumping through Rb makes polarized 3He, which serves as an effective polarized neutron target, and strained GaAs photocathodes deliver ~85–90% polarized electron beams at JLab. These beams made the recoil-polarization measurement of G_E/G_M possible, which revealed its disagreement with Rosenbluth separation.

name: Reactor criticality as a Helmholtz eigenproblem
summary: In one-group diffusion theory the critical reactor flux satisfies the Helmholtz equation ∇^2φ + B^2φ = 0. Its fundamental shapes (cos, J_0, sin(πr/R)/r) and geometric buckling eigenvalues are the same as the cavity-mode solutions of electromagnetism. Criticality means the material buckling (k∞ − 1)/L^2 equals the geometric buckling.
breaks: φ is a diffusing density, not a wave, so there is no phase or interference. Boundary conditions apply at an extrapolated surface rather than at conducting walls, and only the fundamental mode survives while higher harmonics decay.

name: RF and crab cavities for the EIC
summary: Electron and ion beams at CEBAF, RHIC and the EIC are accelerated and bunched by the TM010 modes of resonant cavities, many of them superconducting. The EIC adds crab cavities, transverse-deflecting modes that tilt the bunches so they collide head-on despite a 25 mrad crossing angle.

name: Spin vs orbital split of photon and gluon angular momentum
summary: Splitting a gauge field's angular momentum into spin and orbital parts depends on the gauge, and the problem is the same for the photon (optical spin versus orbital angular momentum) and the gluon (ΔG versus L_g in the proton spin budget). The Jaffe–Manohar (canonical) and Ji (kinetic, gauge-invariant) decompositions correspond to canonical versus kinetic momentum under minimal coupling p → p − qA.
map: \mathbf J_\gamma=\epsilon_0\int[\mathbf E\times\mathbf A_\perp+E_i(\mathbf r\times\nabla)A_{\perp i}]d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ \tfrac12=\tfrac12\Delta\Sigma+\Delta G+L_q+L_g
sources: European Muon Collaboration (1988). "A measurement of the spin asymmetry and determination of the structure function g1 in deep inelastic muon-proton scattering". *Phys. Lett. B* 206, 364. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7)

name: Equivalent-photon approximation for photoproduction
summary: The Lorentz-contracted field of a fast charge is equivalent to a flux of quasi-real photons proportional to Z^2α (Fermi 1924, Weizsäcker–Williams 1934). This underlies photoproduction at the EIC (Q^2 → 0) and the photonuclear and photon–photon physics of ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC, which serve as EIC precursors.

name: Ultrastrong magnetic fields in heavy-ion collisions
summary: In off-central collisions the Lorentz-contracted Liénard–Wiechert fields of the spectator protons produce eB ~ m_π^2 (~10^14 T), the strongest magnetic fields known. They last a few fm/c, extended by Faraday induction in the conducting QGP. These fields drive searches for the chiral magnetic effect and for charge splittings in directed flow and Λ polarization; the 2022 STAR isobar blind analysis found no predefined CME signature.
map: B\simeq\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{Ze\gamma v}{b^2},\ \ eB\sim m_\pi^2\ (\sim10^{14}\ \mathrm T);\ \ \mathbf J_{\rm CME}=\frac{e^2}{2\pi^2}\mu_5\mathbf B\ (\text{natural units})

name: Spin–orbit coupling: atomic vs nuclear
summary: Atomic spin–orbit coupling comes from the magnetic field in the electron's rest frame, with the Thomas factor ½. Mayer and Jensen's strong nuclear spin–orbit term, which produces the magic numbers, has the same L·S form. In relativistic mean-field theory it comes out of the same Dirac reduction, applied to the large scalar and vector nuclear potentials.
map: H_{so}^{\rm at}=\frac{1}{2m^2c^2}\frac{1}{r}\frac{dV}{dr}\mathbf L\cdot\mathbf S\ \leftrightarrow\ H_{so}^{\rm nuc}\propto\frac{1}{r}\frac{d(V-S)}{dr}\mathbf l\cdot\mathbf s
breaks: The nuclear term is not electromagnetic and is far larger relative to level spacings. Its sign lowers j = l + ½ and creates intruder states, while in atoms spin–orbit is a fine-structure correction of order α^2 with the opposite ordering.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)

name: Coulomb barrier and electron screening in fusion
summary: Fusion and α-decay rates are set by tunnelling through the electrostatic barrier Z1Z2e^2/4πε0r, so the Gamow factor exp(-2πη) is pure Coulomb physics. Atomic electrons screen the bare charge and raise low-energy laboratory cross sections by exp(πηU_e/E); this must be removed before S-factors are used for stars, where plasma (Debye) screening takes its place. Measured screening potentials often exceed the adiabatic electrostatic estimate.
map: V_C=\frac{Z_1Z_2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0r},\ \ \eta=\frac{Z_1Z_2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar v},\ \ \frac{\sigma_{\rm scr}}{\sigma_{\rm bare}}\approx e^{\pi\eta U_e/E}
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)

name: Coulomb energy of a charged drop sets the fission limit
summary: The Coulomb term of the semi-empirical mass formula is the electrostatic self-energy of a uniformly charged sphere. Bohr–Wheeler fission theory balances it against surface tension for l=2 shape deformations, which gives the fissility x = E_C/2E_S and the liquid-drop limit Z^2/A ≈ 50. This is the nuclear version of Rayleigh's 1882 instability of a charged conducting droplet.
breaks: A conducting drop carries surface charge while the nucleus carries volume charge, so the critical ratios differ. Real fission barriers, spontaneous fission and the existence of superheavy elements beyond x≈1 come from quantum shell corrections and tunnelling, not from classical electrostatics.
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)
Weizsäcker (1935). "Zur Theorie der Kernmassen". *Z. Phys.* 96, 431. [doi:10.1007/BF01337700](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01337700)

name: Yukawa potential as a screened Coulomb Green's function
summary: Yukawa built the nuclear force by giving the electrostatic field a mass. The static potential is the Green's function of the screened Poisson equation and reduces to Coulomb's law as μ→0; its range ħ/m_πc ≈ 1.4 fm predicted the pion. One-pion exchange is still the long-range part of every modern chiral-EFT potential.
breaks: The pion is a pseudoscalar isovector, so one-pion exchange has spin–isospin and tensor structure that Coulomb's law lacks. The short-range core, two-pion exchange and three-nucleon forces have no electrostatic analogue.
sources: Yukawa (1935). "On the Interaction of Elementary Particles. I". *Proc. Phys.-Math. Soc. Jpn.* 17, 48. [doi:10.11429/ppmsj1919.17.0_48](https://doi.org/10.11429/ppmsj1919.17.0_48)

name: Fermi density effect in ionization energy loss
summary: At high βγ the polarization of the medium screens distant collisions and reduces the relativistic rise of the Bethe stopping power by the density-effect term δ. δ depends on the medium's dielectric response through its plasma frequency. Fermi's 1940 dielectric treatment showed that the same polarization field radiates Cherenkov light wherever ε(ω) > 1/β^2.

name: Debye screening of colour and quarkonium melting
summary: Free colour charges screen the static quark–antiquark potential the same way mobile charges screen a Coulomb field, with dielectric function ε(k) = 1 + m_D^2/k^2. Heavy quarkonia therefore dissolve once the Debye length becomes smaller than their size. Matsui and Satz proposed J/ψ suppression as a QGP signature on this basis.
breaks: Colour is non-Abelian and magnetic screening is non-perturbative. The imaginary part of the in-medium potential (Landau damping) dominates dissociation, and at the LHC charm quarks recombine to regenerate J/ψ.
sources: Matsui & Satz (1986). "J/ψ suppression by quark-gluon plasma formation". *Phys. Lett. B* 178, 416. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8)

name: MAC-E filter: adiabatic magnetic collimation in KATRIN
summary: KATRIN's MAC-E filter uses a slowly varying magnetic field, so the adiabatic invariant p_⊥^2/B turns almost all transverse momentum of tritium β electrons into longitudinal motion against an electrostatic retarding potential. This gives an energy resolution ΔE/E = B_min/B_max and sub-eV limits on the neutrino mass.

name: Flow eccentricities as multipole moments of the fireball
summary: The initial shape of the fireball is decomposed into azimuthal multipole moments of its entropy density, the eccentricities ε_n, and hydrodynamics turns them almost linearly into flow harmonics v_n. A deformed nucleus adds its quadrupole (β_2) to ε_2, so flow data now image the deformation of 238U and 129Xe. This links back to nuclear quadrupole moments.
map: \varepsilon_ne^{in\Phi_n}=-\frac{\int r^ne^{in\phi}s(\mathbf r)\,d^2r}{\int r^ns(\mathbf r)\,d^2r},\ \ v_n\approx\kappa_n\varepsilon_n,\ \ \langle\varepsilon_2^2\rangle\approx a+b\beta_2^2
breaks: These are 2D cylindrical moments of an entropy density, not 3D spherical moments of a charge. The response is viscous and partly non-linear rather than a static field.

name: Nuclear multipole moments and deformation
summary: Nuclear charge and current distributions are described by the same spherical multipoles as in electrostatics. Magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments test the shell model (Schmidt lines, single-particle Q), and the intrinsic quadrupole of a deformed nucleus is the l=2 multipole of its surface. Both are measured through the quadrupole–field-gradient coupling in atomic hyperfine structure and through Coulomb-excitation B(E2) values.

name: Laser isotope separation
summary: When isotope shifts exceed the Doppler width, narrow-band lasers can selectively ionize or dissociate one isotope (AVLIS on atomic vapour, molecular schemes on UF6). The technique is used for uranium enrichment, for laser-ionized radioactive beams, and increasingly for medical-isotope precursors.

name: Muonic-hydrogen laser spectroscopy of the proton radius
summary: Pulsed laser spectroscopy of the 2S–2P Lamb shift in muonic hydrogen, at about 6 μm, gave a proton charge radius of 0.84 fm, ten times more precise than before; it started the proton-radius puzzle. Frequency-comb spectroscopy of ordinary hydrogen and new electron-scattering data now largely agree with it.
sources: Pohl et al. (2010). "The size of the proton". *Nature* 466, 213. [doi:10.1038/nature09250](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09250)

name: Laser-driven inertial fusion of D–T
summary: Inertial confinement fusion uses lasers as the driver. NIF's 192 frequency-tripled (351 nm) Nd:glass beams heat a hohlraum whose X-rays implode a D–T capsule, and since December 2022 some shots have released more fusion energy than the laser energy delivered to the target. Nonlinear-optical frequency conversion, beam smoothing and laser–plasma instabilities set the performance limits.

name: Laser spectroscopy of radii and moments of rare isotopes
summary: Collinear and resonance-ionization laser spectroscopy measure the spins, magnetic and quadrupole moments and charge radii of short-lived isotopes from hyperfine structure and isotope shifts. The results reveal shell closures, halos and unexpected radius trends such as the large radii of neutron-rich calcium, and the method has reached nobelium. Resonance laser ion sources also provide element-selective radioactive beams.

name: Giant dipole resonance as a nuclear plasmon
summary: The giant dipole resonance, in which protons oscillate against neutrons, is a nuclear analogue of the localized surface plasmon of a metal nanoparticle. Both are a single Lorentzian collective dipole mode that exhausts the dipole sum rule (Thomas–Reiche–Kuhn in nuclei, the f-sum rule in optics). Metal-cluster physicists describe the cluster's Mie plasmon in the same language.
breaks: The restoring force is the nuclear symmetry energy, not Coulomb attraction, and both fluids move. The GDR energy falls with size (~A^-1/3), whereas the quasi-static plasmon frequency ω_p/√3 does not depend on size.

name: Light-by-light scattering in ultraperipheral collisions
summary: The QED vacuum's Euler–Heisenberg four-photon coupling is the vacuum analogue of an optical χ^(3) Kerr nonlinearity. It was first seen as light-by-light scattering γγ → γγ in ultra-peripheral Pb–Pb collisions, using the quasi-real photon clouds of the nuclei (ATLAS evidence 2017, later CMS and ATLAS observations). The related Breit–Wheeler process γγ → e+e− is also measured there.
map: \mathcal L_{\rm EH}=\frac{2\alpha^2}{45m_e^4}\big[(\mathbf E^2-\mathbf B^2)^2+7(\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B)^2\big]\ \ (\text{natural units})
breaks: The Euler–Heisenberg Lagrangian is only the low-energy limit ω ≪ m_e, and UPC photon pairs at GeV energies probe the full box diagram. Laser vacuum-birefringence searches such as PVLAS have not yet reached the effective-Lagrangian signal.
